themes.theme: Middle East escalation and Saudi infrastructure risk
themes.summary: Houthi strikes on Saudi assets, 29 Iranian ship attacks in October and a disabled tanker keep a risk premium in place, with CERA saying Iran, Houthis and Iraqi militias can all threaten oil infrastructure.
Hormuz transits steady at 17 with six VLCCs on Oct 25, CENTCOM says 1.5 billion barrels have exited, and Middle East exports are about 74% of pre-war levels, easing sour differentials.
Brent fell 91 cents to $115.81/b and WTI $1.51 to $101.76/b on Oct 26 as traders booked profits and watched US-Iran diplomacy.

themes.theme: Record freight and Atlantic/Med sweet weakness
themes.summary: Record VLCC and Black Sea freight and ample supply pushed CPC Blend to record-low differentials and capped arbitrage, while WAF and North Sea differentials stay soft.
US crude stocks seen drawing a fourth week to about 411.3 million bbl with runs at 93.6%, while global onshore stocks are under 6 billion barrels per Aramco's CEO.

themes.theme: Rerouting of Saudi/Gulf crude and storage
themes.summary: Saudi barrels flow via Yanbu, Suez and SUMED, Aramco is pricing against ICE Brent, and a Singapore storage MOU is set; Saudi supply recovery weighs on sours and Urals.
US waivers sustain Russian crude flows to India and China and reopen Russian diesel to the US, while Ukrainian drones keep 3.1 million b/d of Russian refining offline.

themes.theme: China product-export cuts and weak refining margins
themes.summary: Chinese refiners plan lower November runs and exports as freight costs make margins negative, with gasoil stocks at the lowest since January 2023.
